t:
Section 103(d) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 113(d)) is amended—
    (1) by striking paragraph (3); and 
    (2) redesignating paragraphs (4) and (5) as paragraphs (3) and (4), respectively.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that strikes one paragraph of the Homeland Security Act and renumbers the remaining paragraphs. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. There is no tempting participation reading here, since no outside party is involved in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that renumbers paragraphs in a statute. It does not create any new process for consultation, public comment, or interaction with outside parties. It merely changes the structure of the text.
qwen_block.s: Section 103(d) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 113(d)) is amended— (1) by striking paragraph (3); and (2) redesignating paragraphs (4) and (5) as paragraphs (3) and (4), respectively.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment: it strikes paragraph (3) of 6 U.S.C. 113(d) and renumbers the remaining paragraphs. It requires no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The fact that it amends a homeland security statute does not bring anyone outside the government into a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Because the text amends the Homeland Security Act, it may seem to affect how the department makes decisions. That reading fails. Section 103(d) lists department officers, and this text only strikes one paragraph and renumbers the rest. No one outside the federal government is consulted, invited to comment, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that strikes and redesignates paragraphs of another statute. It does not itself create, require, or describe any process for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with parties outside the government. The text contains no references to public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, consultation with states/tribes, or rights to sue. It is purely a legislative housekeeping provision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 103(d) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 113(d)) is amended— (1) by striking paragraph (3); and (2) redesignating paragraphs (4) and (5) as paragraphs (3) and (4), respectively.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section amends a statute that likely contains provisions about participation (like advisory committees or public comment), the amendment itself is related to participation. However, the text provided is purely a technical amendment (striking and redesignating paragraphs) and does not itself establish, require, or describe any process of consultation, coordination, or input from outside the federal government. It is a structural change to the code, not a substantive mandate for participation.
